decision: Accept byte-identical observations from two fresh frozen-original processes and the retained v0.27.1 installed adapter, before implementing a request-preflight runtime. No diagnostic projection or expected-result regeneration was used.
scope: 68 request courses and 71 transitions, including competing gates, native hive possession/ejection, authored Gnatveil transit investment, passive replenishment, real workshop deployment/relocation, explicit body/resource state and labelled synthetic definition combinations.
correctionsBeforeAcceptance: An initial interaction test assumed native Mimicry had attribute requirements. The original registry proves it does not. Its successful low-attribute redirect is now preserved explicitly; an attribute-bearing Firebolt carrying the original mimic trait separately tests attribute-before-mimic ordering. The failing test assumption emitted no accepted fixture and changed no game code.
limitations: Forwarding observers call the actual World methods and actor canUse; they do not replace decisions. Their meaningful call order, state and results compare without projection.

Some actor flags, banks and rule combinations are explicitly seeded to isolate precedence. Native aura activation, tree spending, possession, deployment and device movement use actual game operations.

Only the proposed sixteen-statement request prefix is the next extraction boundary. Reserve spending, combo commitment, random fumble/scramble, targeting, paid mode preparation and general effect delivery remain host-owned.
A successful request may be a toggle or redirect; it does not prove a cast began or an effect landed.
No renderer, physical input, performance, allocation, target-device or new native-engine capability is established by this baseline.
